text: ggplot2 installed, autoplot() draws fan chart ggplot object, usual ggplot2 modifications apply. autolayer() adds forecast bands median existing plot. natural use backtest. Hold last three years, forecast , overlay actually happened: well calibrated intervals ? share held-months inside central interval:
code: autoplot(fc) +   labs(title = "AirPassengers", y = "Passengers (thousands)") train <- window(AirPassengers, end = c(1957, 12)) test  <- window(AirPassengers, start = c(1958, 1)) fc_bt <- timestral_forecast(m, train, h = length(test))  actual <- data.frame(time = as.numeric(time(AirPassengers)),                      value = as.numeric(AirPassengers),                      part = ifelse(time(AirPassengers) < 1958,                                    "training data", "held out")) ggplot(actual, aes(time, value)) +   autolayer(fc_bt) +   geom_line(aes(colour = part), linewidth = 0.5) +   scale_colour_manual(values = c("training data" = "black",                                  "held out" = "#D55E00"), name = NULL) +   labs(title = "Backtest: forecasting 1958-1960 from data up to 1957",        x = NULL, y = "Passengers (thousands)") q <- fc_bt$quantiles[1, , ] lv <- fc_bt$levels inside <- function(p) {   lo <- q[, which.min(abs(lv - (1 - p) / 2))]   hi <- q[, which.min(abs(lv - (1 + p) / 2))]   mean(test >= lo & test <= hi) } data.frame(interval = c("50%", "80%", "90%", "98%"),            coverage = sapply(c(0.5, 0.8, 0.9, 0.98), inside)) #>   interval coverage #> 1      50%   0.5000 #> 2      80%   0.8333 #> 3      90%   0.9722 #> 4      98%   1.0000

title: Probabilistic forecasting with timestralR
text: Timestral can condition covariates three kinds: past_covariates: known context (T rows), leading indicator forecast; known_covariates: known context horizon (T + h rows), planned promotions, prices holidays; categorical_past_covariates categorical_known_covariates: integer category codes (weekday, store type, …), target-encoded internally. Covariates passed time rows, one column per covariate. example, simulated daily sales product weekly pattern occasional promotions lift sales 60%. promotion calendar planned, also known 8 weeks want forecast. Without covariates model sees spikes history know next ones happen. Passing promotion calendar known covariate, weekday categorical known covariate, lets place : simple score shows gain, using mean absolute error median mean pinball (quantile) loss 21 levels: Past-covariates use row layout context , example past_covariates = cbind(footfall = footfall[1:n_ctx]). batch, give list one covariate matrix per series.
code: n_ctx <- 364; h <- 56; n <- n_ctx + h day <- seq_len(n) weekday <- (day - 1) %% 7                       # 0 = Monday promo <- as.numeric(runif(n) < 0.12) promo[n_ctx + c(5, 6, 19, 20, 33, 34, 47, 48)] <- 1  # planned promotions base <- 100 + 0.05 * day + c(0, -5, -5, 0, 10, 25, 15)[weekday + 1] sales <- base * (1 + 0.6 * promo) * exp(rnorm(n, sd = 0.05))  y_ctx <- sales[seq_len(n_ctx)] ggplot(data.frame(day = day, sales = sales, promo = factor(promo)),        aes(day, sales)) +   geom_line(colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.3) +   geom_point(aes(colour = promo), size = 0.7) +   geom_vline(xintercept = n_ctx + 0.5, linetype = 2) +   scale_colour_manual(values = c("0" = "grey40", "1" = "#D55E00"),                       labels = c("regular day", "promotion"), name = NULL) +   labs(title = "Simulated daily sales; the dashed line ends the context",        x = "Day", y = "Sales") fc_plain <- timestral_forecast(m, y_ctx, h = h) fc_cov <- timestral_forecast(   m, y_ctx, h = h,   known_covariates = cbind(promo = promo),   categorical_known_covariates = cbind(weekday = weekday) ) cov_panel <- function(f, title) {   qs <- f$quantiles[1, , ]   d <- data.frame(day = n_ctx + seq_len(h), actual = sales[n_ctx + seq_len(h)],                   lo = qs[, "0.10"], hi = qs[, "0.90"], med = qs[, "0.50"])   hist <- data.frame(day = (n_ctx - 55):n_ctx, sales = y_ctx[(n_ctx - 55):n_ctx])   ggplot(d, aes(day)) +     geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), fill = "#6BAED6", alpha = 0.5) +     geom_line(data = hist, aes(day, sales), colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.4) +     geom_line(aes(y = med), colour = "#08519C", linewidth = 0.6) +     geom_point(aes(y = actual), colour = "#D55E00", size = 0.9) +     labs(subtitle = title, x = "Day", y = "Sales") } cov_panel(fc_plain, "no covariates") /   cov_panel(fc_cov, "promotion calendar + weekday as known covariates") +   plot_annotation(     title = "Median and 80% interval; dots are the held-out actuals") actual <- sales[n_ctx + seq_len(h)] pinball <- function(f) {   qs <- f$quantiles[1, , ]   mean(sapply(seq_along(f$levels), function(j) {     e <- actual - qs[, j]     mean(pmax(f$levels[j] * e, (f$levels[j] - 1) * e))   })) } data.frame(   model = c("no covariates", "with covariates"),   MAE = c(mean(abs(actual - fc_plain$quantiles[1, , "0.50"])),           mean(abs(actual - fc_cov$quantiles[1, , "0.50"]))),   pinball = c(pinball(fc_plain), pinball(fc_cov)) ) #>             model    MAE pinball #> 1   no covariates 21.483   7.613 #> 2 with covariates  7.586   2.634

text: timestral_score() scores forecast values later observed, one row per step. Besides absolute error median (ae) reports two scores whole predictive distribution: pinball (quantile) loss averaged 21 levels (pinball), approximation continuous ranked probability score (crps). also reports whether step fell inside 80% 98% intervals. Lower scores better, point forecast distribution scores reduce () absolute error. section 2 backtest, scored: One held-window says little. timestral_backtest() repeats forecast several origins, time using data origin, scores every forecast. origin moves forward year time last six years AirPassengers, 12-month horizon time: Averaging forecast step shows accuracy falls horizon: Covariates observation_mask passed whole series cut origin: past-covariates mask context, known-future covariates context plus horizon. list equal-length series backtested batch origin. backtest runs one origin another; spread origins cores, split run one backtest per chunk (see ?timestral_backtest next section). tsibbles, fable route covers ground: tsibble::stretch_tsibble(), TIMESTRAL() model accuracy().

text: main options timestral_forecast(): symmetric = TRUE (default) averages forecast mirrored series (-y), removes sign bias; clip_nonnegative = TRUE (default) clips quantiles zero every observed value non-negative. timestral_load() controls decoding: max_context caps context length (default trained context length); per_shot_horizon_patches sets many 32-step patches decoded per block median fed back long horizons; quantile_real_cap_k extreme_value_threshold safety clamps extreme inputs.

code: library(timestralR) m  <- timestral_load("28M")                  # or a local directory or Hub repo ID fc <- timestral_forecast(m, AirPassengers, h = 24) plot(fc)                                     # fan chart: history + median + bands timestral_median(fc)                         # a ts, starting Jan 1961 timestral_quantile(fc, 0.9)                  # any of fc$levels fc$quantiles                                 # array: variate x step x 21 levels head(as_forecast_df(fc))                     # tidy long format (with time column) # multivariate: columns are forecast jointly fc2 <- timestral_forecast(m, cbind(mdeaths, fdeaths), h = 12)  # a batch of independent series in one call fcb <- timestral_forecast(m, list(a = mdeaths, b = fdeaths), h = 12)  # covariates, time in rows: past-only over the context, known-future over # the context plus the horizon (T + h rows) y <- as.numeric(AirPassengers) x <- seq_len(length(y) + 12) fc3 <- timestral_forecast(m, y, h = 12,                           past_covariates = log(y),                           known_covariates = cbind(trend = x),                           categorical_known_covariates = (x - 1) %% 12)

title: Score quantile forecasts against realised values — timestral_score
text: scores, realised value \(y\) quantile \(q_\tau\) level \(\tau\) forecast (fc$levels), use pinball (quantile) loss \(\rho_\tau = (1\{y < q_\tau\} - \tau)(q_\tau - y)\): pinball: \(2\rho_\tau\) averaged levels, quantile loss used GluonTS Chronos benchmarks (dividing scale series). factor 2 makes equal absolute error point forecast. crps: continuous ranked probability score, \(2\int_0^1 \rho_\tau\,d\tau\), approximated trapezoidal rule knots. knots evenly spaced, weighted spacing rather averaged. integral covers knots' range (0.01 0.99 official checkpoints), point forecast gives \(0.98|q - y|\) rather \(|q - y|\): tails beyond outermost knots ignored. ae: absolute error median. cover<L>: whether \(y\) lies central L% interval, level; level must pair two knots, plot(). Missing actual values give missing scores. Average rows stats::aggregate() dplyr summarise step, series origin.
